en: To cause someone to become hostile or annoyed
bn: বিরূপ করে তোলা; শত্রুতা সৃষ্টি করা
hook: ANTAGONIZE: turn someone into your ANTAGONIST (enemy).
story: Antagonize. Nadia's new flatmate began by borrowing her shampoo without asking. Then she played loud music at midnight, mocked Nadia's cooking in front of guests, and parked her bicycle across Nadia's door. Within a month, the once friendly Nadia would not even say hello. Her flatmate had antagonized her: caused her to become hostile and annoyed. An antagonist is an opponent, like the villain of a film. Synonyms: provoke, alienate, offend.

gre.s: Eager not to ____ the powerful landlords whose support he needed, the reformer softened his proposals until they offended no one.
gre.clue: until they offended no one

en: Unable to produce crops, offspring, or results; empty
hook: BARREN: as empty as a BARREL with nothing inside.
story: Barren. After the river changed course, the fields of Shuvo's village turned to dry, cracked earth. Farmers planted rice, then wheat, then lentils, but nothing would grow. The land had become barren: unable to produce crops. Barren can also describe a woman or animal unable to have offspring, or anything empty of results, like a barren discussion that leads nowhere. Opposite: fertile, fruitful. Synonyms: infertile, sterile, desolate.

gre.s: Years of intensive farming without rest had left the once fertile valley ____, its exhausted soil yielding barely enough to feed the families who tilled it.
gre.clue: its exhausted soil yielding barely enough

en: Using pompous, inflated language with little meaning
hook: BOMBASTIC: words that sound like a BOMB but carry nothing.
story: Bombastic. At the village election rally, the candidate grabbed the microphone and roared, 'I shall be the sun that illuminates the eternal darkness of our glorious destiny!' He spoke for an hour in this style, and nobody could say what he had actually promised. His speech was bombastic: pompous and inflated, with little meaning. Bombast originally meant cotton stuffing used to pad clothes, so bombastic words are stuffed to look bigger. Synonyms: pompous, grandiloquent, overblown.

gre.s: Reviewers mocked the memoir's ____ prose, in which even a trip to the grocery store became an epic struggle described in grandiose, ornate language.
gre.clue: described in grandiose, ornate language

en: To persuade someone through flattery or gentle, persistent coaxing
bn: তোষামোদ করে রাজি করানো; ভুলিয়ে-ভালিয়ে রাজি করানো
hook: CAJOLE: CAGE them with sweet words, JOLLY them along.
story: Cajole. Little Tania wanted ice cream before dinner, and her father said no. So she climbed onto his lap, told him he was the best father in Bangladesh, rubbed his tired shoulders, and asked sweetly, again and again, for just one small cone. Twenty minutes later they were walking to the shop. She had cajoled him: persuaded him through flattery and gentle, persistent coaxing. Cajole and wheedle are near twins. Synonyms: coax, sweet-talk.

gre.s: Unable to force the stubborn witness to testify, the detective tried instead to ____ him, offering compliments and small favors until he agreed to talk.
gre.clue: offering compliments and small favors

en: Cautious and wary; reluctant to give or risk
hook: CHARY: CAREFUL and wARY.
story: Chary. Tanvir once lent his notes to a classmate, who copied them, submitted them as his own, and got Tanvir accused of plagiarism. Since then, Tanvir is chary of lending anything. He asks questions, hesitates, and usually says no. He is chary: cautious and wary, reluctant to give or risk. Chary is related to care, so a chary person is careful. Being chary of praise means giving it rarely. Synonyms: wary, cautious, leery.

gre.s: Having lost heavily in the last market crash, investors were understandably ____ of new technology stocks, refusing to commit money without years of proven profits.
gre.clue: refusing to commit money without years of proven profits

en: A bad-tempered, grumpy person, especially an old one
hook: CURMUDGEON: a grumpy old CUR (dog) growling in the MUD.
story: Curmudgeon. Old Mr Karim in flat 3B complains about everything. The children are too noisy, the lift is too slow, the tea is too sweet, and modern music is a crime. When neighbours wish him a happy Eid, he grumbles that holidays are a waste of time. He is a curmudgeon: a bad-tempered, grumpy person, especially an old one. Picture a snarling cur, a stray dog, muttering at everyone who passes. Synonyms: grouch, crank, grump.

gre.s: Though he cultivated a reputation as a ____, grumbling at visitors and scowling in photographs, the old professor quietly paid the tuition of dozens of poor students.
gre.clue: grumbling at visitors and scowling in photographs

en: A mournful song or lament for the dead
hook: DIRGE: sung at a funeral, with a slow, sad DRAG.
story: Dirge. When the old fisherman of the village died, his friends carried his body to the riverbank at dusk. As the boat moved slowly through the water, the women sang a slow, sorrowful song of farewell, and even the children fell silent. That song was a dirge: a mournful song or lament for the dead. The word comes from a Latin funeral chant beginning with dirige. Any slow, gloomy music may be called a dirge. Synonyms: lament, elegy.

gre.s: The band's usually upbeat anthem sounded like a ____ that night: played slowly and softly in memory of their late drummer, it moved the entire stadium to tears.
gre.clue: in memory of their late drummer

en: Worthy of great respect
hook: ESTIMABLE: held in high ESTEEM.
story: Estimable. For forty years, Dr Tania Rahman ran a free clinic in a remote char village, treating thousands of patients and refusing every offer of a city job. When she retired, the whole district came to thank her. She was an estimable woman: worthy of great respect. Estimable shares a root with esteem, so think of someone held in high esteem. On the GRE it rarely means able to be estimated. Synonyms: admirable, respected, worthy.

gre.s: Despite their political differences, even the senator's rivals regarded him as thoroughly ____, a public servant whose integrity had never once been questioned.
gre.clue: whose integrity had never once been questioned

en: A mild word substituted for one considered harsh or blunt
hook: EU-PHEMISM: EU = good, PHEME = speech. Good-sounding speech.
story: Euphemism. When Rafi lost his job, the company's letter said he had been released to pursue other opportunities. When his grandfather died, relatives said he had passed away. And when the government raised taxes, it called them revenue enhancements. Each phrase is a euphemism: a mild word substituted for a harsh or blunt one. In Greek, eu means good and pheme means speech, so a euphemism is good-sounding speech. Its opposite is a dysphemism, a deliberately harsh term.

gre.s: Calling the mass layoffs a 'workforce optimization' was a transparent ____, a gentle phrase designed to disguise the harsh reality that thousands had lost their jobs.
gre.clue: a gentle phrase designed to disguise the harsh reality

en: To criticize very severely
hook: EX-CORIATE: to strip off the skin (corium), with harsh words.
story: Excoriate. A new bridge in a northern town cracked only six months after it opened. At the public hearing, an engineer stood up and tore the construction company apart: cheap steel, stolen funds, ignored warnings, and lies to the press. For an hour he spared nothing. He excoriated the company: he criticized it very severely. Literally, excoriate means to strip off the skin, from the Latin corium, meaning hide. Such criticism feels like being skinned. Synonyms: lambaste, castigate, berate.

gre.s: Reviewers did not merely criticize the novel; they chose to ____ it, condemning its plot, its prose, and its author's integrity in the harshest possible terms.
gre.clue: in the harshest possible terms

en: Pressing; demanding immediate action
hook: EXIGENT: an EMERGENT, EXTREME need.
story: Exigent. At two in the morning, the river embankment near Sirajganj began to give way. Water was seeping through, and three villages lay behind it. There was no time for meetings or permits; volunteers grabbed sandbags in the dark. The situation was exigent: pressing, demanding immediate action. The noun is exigency, an urgent need. Exigent can also describe a demanding person, like an exigent boss who wants everything yesterday. Synonyms: urgent, pressing, critical.

gre.s: Because the circumstances were so ____, with the floodwaters rising by the hour, officials bypassed the usual approval process and evacuated the town at once.
gre.clue: with the floodwaters rising by the hour

en: Arrogantly superior and disdainful
hook: HAUGHTY: HIGH and mighty, nose in the air.
story: Haughty. At the school reunion, Imran's old classmate arrived in a new car, looked around the simple restaurant, and wrinkled his nose. He refused to shake hands with the waiter, talked only about his villa in Gulshan, and called his former friends you village people. He was haughty: arrogantly superior and disdainful. Haughty comes from an old word for high, so a haughty person holds his head high and looks down on others. Synonyms: arrogant, supercilious, condescending.

gre.s: The heiress was so ____ that she refused even to acknowledge the servants, addressing them only through her secretary as though they were beneath her notice.
gre.clue: as though they were beneath her notice

en: Having a strong, exciting, intoxicating effect
hook: HEADY: goes straight to your HEAD.
story: Heady. The night Bangladesh beat a cricket giant in a World Cup match, Dhaka exploded. Strangers hugged in the streets, horns honked until dawn, and Anika felt as if she were floating. Those were heady days: exciting, almost intoxicating. Heady means having a strong, exciting effect, like wine that goes straight to the head. A heady perfume is strong, and heady success can make people reckless. Synonyms: exhilarating, intoxicating, thrilling.

gre.s: For the young founders, the first months were ____: glowing press coverage and millions in investment arrived so quickly that they felt almost drunk with success.
gre.clue: felt almost drunk with success

en: Unable to be upset or excited; extremely calm
hook: IM-PERTURB-ABLE: can't be PERTURBED.
story: Imperturbable. The ferry rocked violently in a storm on the Padma. Passengers screamed, bags slid across the deck, and children cried. But the old captain stood at the wheel, sipping his tea and calmly giving orders, as if it were a quiet afternoon. He was imperturbable: unable to be upset or excited, extremely calm. To perturb is to disturb, so imperturbable means impossible to disturb. Synonyms: unflappable, composed, unruffled.

gre.s: The chess champion remained ____ throughout the tournament; neither her opponent's taunts nor the roaring crowd produced so much as a flicker of emotion on her face.
gre.clue: neither her opponent's taunts nor the roaring crowd

en: Unable to be calmed or satisfied; relentless
hook: IM-PLACABLE: can't be PLACATED.
story: Implacable. Two families in a Barisal village have quarrelled over a strip of land for three generations. Elders tried to mediate, the courts ruled, and apologies were offered, but nothing worked. Each side rejects every compromise. Their hatred is implacable: unable to be calmed or satisfied, relentless. To placate is to calm someone down, so implacable means impossible to placate. An implacable enemy never gives up. Synonyms: relentless, unappeasable, unforgiving.

gre.s: No concession seemed enough for the ____ critic, who greeted each revision of the policy with fresh and even fiercer objections.
gre.clue: greeted each revision of the policy with fresh and even fiercer objections

en: To criticize harshly
hook: LAMBASTE: LAMB gets BASTED (beaten) with harsh words.
story: Lambaste. Arif's team submitted a careless project report, full of copied paragraphs and wrong numbers. In the next meeting, the department head lambasted them in front of everyone. She listed every error, called the work disgraceful, and demanded a full rewrite by Monday. To lambaste is to criticize harshly. The word joins two old verbs that both meant to beat, lam and baste. It is close to excoriate. Synonyms: berate, castigate, slam.

gre.s: Rather than praising the minister's long-delayed reforms, opposition leaders chose to ____ them as too little, too late, and a betrayal of earlier promises.
gre.clue: too little, too late, and a betrayal of earlier promises

en: A person who behaves badly or breaks the law
hook: MIS-CREANT: a MIS-CREATED person who does wrong.
story: Miscreant. Every night for a month, someone slashed the tyres of motorcycles parked outside Rafi's building. The guards were puzzled and the residents furious, until a hidden camera caught the culprit: a teenager from the next street who did it for fun. The police called him a miscreant: a person who behaves badly or breaks the law. Bangladeshi newspapers often use the word for unidentified criminals. Mis means wrong. Synonyms: wrongdoer, villain, delinquent.

gre.s: The townspeople regarded the young man as a hopeless ____ until he returned the stolen money and spent years volunteering to repay his debt to the community.
gre.clue: returned the stolen money

en: A small, relatively unimportant sin or fault
hook: PECCADILLO: a tiny sin, small as an armadillo.
story: Peccadillo. Babu's grandmother caught him sneaking an extra mishti from the kitchen before the guests arrived. She pretended to be angry, then laughed and gave him another. It was only a peccadillo: a small, relatively unimportant sin or fault. Peccadillo comes from the Spanish for little sin, from the same Latin root as impeccable, meaning without flaw. Voters may forgive a politician's peccadilloes but not his crimes. Synonyms: lapse, indiscretion.

gre.s: Supporters dismissed the scandal as a mere ____, but investigators soon showed that the senator's misconduct was neither minor nor isolated.
gre.clue: dismissed the scandal as a mere

en: A person hostile or indifferent to culture and the arts
hook: PHILISTINE: thinks a museum is a waste of land.
story: Philistine. When the town council planned to demolish a two-hundred-year-old zamindar palace to build a parking lot, Ishita protested. One councillor shrugged: 'Old buildings, paintings, poetry, what use are they? They make no money.' Ishita called him a philistine: a person hostile or indifferent to culture and the arts. The name comes from an ancient people portrayed in the Bible as enemies of the Israelites. Opposite: aesthete. Synonyms: boor, barbarian.

gre.s: Dismissing the museum as a waste of public money, the mayor revealed himself to be a ____, indifferent to the paintings and sculptures that had made the city famous.
gre.clue: indifferent to the paintings and sculptures

en: To move to a lower or less important position
hook: RELEGATE: sent back to the LEAGUE below.
story: Relegate. Lamia was the star of her university football team, until a new coach arrived who disliked her. He moved her to the bench, then to the reserve squad, and finally gave her the job of collecting balls. He had relegated her: moved her to a lower or less important position. In European football, a team that finishes last is relegated to a lower division. Re means back and legare means to send. Synonyms: demote, downgrade, consign.

gre.s: Although she was once celebrated as a pioneer, younger scholars now tend to ____ her work to footnotes, considering her methods hopelessly outdated.
gre.clue: considering her methods hopelessly outdated

en: Extremely distasteful; disgusting
hook: REPUGNANT: makes you REPEL and PUKE.
story: Repugnant. Kamal took a summer job at a trading company, then discovered that his manager was cheating poor farmers with rigged scales. When the manager offered him a bonus to keep quiet, Kamal felt sick. The very idea was repugnant to him: extremely distasteful, disgusting. Repugnant comes from the Latin for fighting back, as if your whole conscience fights against it. Do not confuse it with pungent, a strong smell. Synonyms: repellent, abhorrent, revolting.

gre.s: Although a few found his argument intellectually intriguing, most readers considered the author's defense of slavery morally ____, an idea too abhorrent to be entertained.
gre.clue: an idea too abhorrent to be entertained

en: Driven by tender or nostalgic feelings, sometimes excessively
hook: SENTIMENTAL: ruled by SENTIMENT (feeling).
story: Sentimental. Sara's father refuses to throw away his old Nokia phone. It does not work and the battery is swollen, but it holds the first message Sara ever sent him. He also keeps her childhood drawings in a tin box and cries at every wedding. He is sentimental: driven by tender or nostalgic feelings, sometimes excessively. A sentimental film pushes the audience toward tears with too much sweetness. Opposite: unsentimental, hard-headed. Synonyms: nostalgic, mawkish.

gre.s: The critic faulted the film for being cloyingly ____, relying on tearful reunions and swelling violins rather than on genuine emotional insight.
gre.clue: tearful reunions and swelling violins

en: To waste money, time, or opportunities recklessly
hook: SQUANDER: SQUASH it and wander away.
story: Squander. Zayan received a scholarship of two lakh taka for his master's degree. Instead of paying his fees, he bought a new phone, threw parties for his friends, and took a trip to Cox's Bazar. By the end of the semester the money was gone and the fees were unpaid. He had squandered it: wasted it recklessly. People also squander time, talent and opportunities. Opposite: conserve. Synonyms: waste, fritter away, dissipate.

gre.s: Having inherited a vast fortune, the young heir managed to ____ nearly all of it within a decade, leaving his children with debts instead of an estate.
gre.clue: leaving his children with debts instead of an estate

en: To cheat someone out of money; a fraud
hook: SWINDLE: like a WINDOW that's actually a painting, a trick.
story: Swindle. A smooth-talking man visited Rumana's village promising to send young men to jobs in Dubai. Each family paid him three lakh taka for visas and tickets. On the day of departure he vanished, along with all the money. He had swindled them: cheated them out of their money. Swindle is also a noun, so the whole scheme was a swindle, and the man was a swindler, a con artist. Synonyms: cheat, defraud, con.

gre.s: The so-called investment firm existed only to ____ elderly retirees, promising guaranteed returns before disappearing with their life savings.
gre.clue: disappearing with their life savings

en: Able to be touched; clear and definite, real
hook: TANGIBLE: you can TOUCH it (tangere = to touch).
story: Tangible. For months, Mitu's charity promised a village that it would rebuild the school. The villagers were doubtful; they had heard promises before. Then one morning trucks arrived with bricks and desks, and within weeks there was a new roof and clean water. Finally there were tangible results: real, clear and definite, things you could actually touch. Tangere is Latin for touch, as in tangent. The opposite is intangible, like trust or goodwill. Synonyms: concrete, palpable.

gre.s: Despite years of lofty promises about reform, the government had produced few ____ improvements that ordinary citizens could actually see in their daily lives.
gre.clue: that ordinary citizens could actually see in their daily lives

en: Depravity; wickedness
hook: TURPITUDE: TURNING PUTRID morally.
story: Turpitude. A respected judge in a small town was found to have taken bribes to free murderers while sending innocent poor men to prison. The public was horrified, not only by the crime but by the deep wickedness behind it. Lawyers called it moral turpitude: depravity, wickedness. In law, moral turpitude means conduct that shocks the conscience. Turpis is Latin for shameful or base. Synonyms: depravity, vileness, iniquity.

gre.s: Voters could forgive the mayor's clumsiness and even occasional dishonesty, but his profiting from child labor exposed a degree of ____ they found unforgivable.
gre.clue: his profiting from child labor

en: Complete and unreserved; pure
hook: UN-ALLOYED: pure gold, not mixed into an ALLOY.
story: Unalloyed. When Mahin opened the email saying he had won a full scholarship to study abroad, he screamed, danced around the room, and called his mother, who burst into happy tears. There was no worry and no doubt mixed in, only joy. It was unalloyed delight: complete, unreserved and pure. An alloy is a metal mixed with another, like brass. So unalloyed means not mixed with anything, like pure gold. Synonyms: pure, unmitigated, sheer.

gre.s: Her joy at the verdict was hardly ____, for though her brother had been freed, the real culprit had escaped justice entirely.
gre.clue: though her brother had been freed, the real culprit had escaped justice

en: To offer lower prices than a competitor; to weaken or undermine
bn: কম দামে বিক্রি করা; দুর্বল করা
hook: UNDER-CUT: CUT the price UNDER theirs, or cut UNDER the foundation.
story: Undercut. A new grocery app in Dhaka began selling rice, lentils and oil for ten percent less than every shop in the neighbourhood. Within months, the corner shops had lost half their customers. The app had undercut them: offered lower prices than its competitors. Undercut also means to weaken or undermine, as when one lie undercuts a lawyer's whole case. Literally, it means to cut away from underneath. Synonyms: undersell, undermine, weaken.

gre.s: The witness's repeated contradictions served only to ____ the credibility of the defense, which had built its entire case on his reliability.
gre.clue: repeated contradictions

en: To use flattery or coaxing to get what one wants
hook: WHEEDLE: a WHEEZING, pleading voice, 'pleeease'.
story: Wheedle. Sabbir wanted his elder brother's motorcycle for the weekend, but he did not ask directly. Instead he praised his brother's cooking, ironed his shirts, and kept saying, 'You are so generous, Bhaiya.' By Friday he had the keys. He had wheedled them out of his brother: used flattery and coaxing to get what he wanted. Wheedle and cajole are near twins, though wheedle often hints at slyness. Synonyms: coax, sweet-talk, inveigle.

gre.s: Too proud to demand a raise outright, the clerk tried to ____ one from his employer, praising her leadership at every opportunity and hinting at his financial troubles.
gre.clue: praising her leadership at every opportunity

en: Having a fear or hatred of foreigners
hook: XENO = foreign, PHOBIA = fear.
story: Xenophobic. When a group of foreign workers arrived to build a bridge near a small town, some residents welcomed them with food. Others put up signs saying foreigners go home, refused to sell them rice, and blamed them for every crime. That fear and hatred of outsiders is xenophobic. Xeno is Greek for stranger, and phobia means fear. Xenophobic politicians often blame immigrants for problems they did not cause. Opposite: cosmopolitan. Synonyms: nativist, chauvinistic.

gre.s: Critics warned that the party's ____ rhetoric, which blamed immigrants for every economic problem, would inflame hostility toward the nation's foreign-born residents.
gre.clue: blamed immigrants for every economic problem
